query: where in the cell does that happen
answer:
In plants and algae, photosynthesis happens inside chloroplasts. These are organelles wrapped in a double membrane, and inside them are stacks of flat, disc-shaped sacs called thylakoids [1][2]. The process runs in two stages in two places. The light-dependent reactions happen in the thylakoid membranes, where chlorophyll absorbs light, splits water (which releases oxygen) and makes ATP and NADPH [1][3]. Those energy carriers then move into the stroma, the fluid around the thylakoids. There the Calvin cycle uses them to turn carbon dioxide into sugar [1][3]. Photosynthetic bacteria like cyanobacteria don't have chloroplasts. They carry out the same reactions on internal membranes in their cytoplasm, and chloroplasts are thought to have evolved from bacteria like these.

Sources:
[1] Light-Dependent and Light-Independent Reactions – https://www.visiblebody.com/learn/biology/photosynthesis/reactions
[2] The Chloroplast (CK-12) – https://flexbooks.ck12.org/cbook/ck-12-cbse-biology-class-11/section/11.4/primary/lesson/the-chloroplast/
